slides.texte_overlay:
7 office social tricks that
feel almost unfair
Learn the names of the people who keep the building running. Reception, security, cleaners. "Morning, Ahmed." They know everything, and they help the people who treat them well.
Send a short recap after every meeting. Three lines, who does what by when. People start seeing you as the organised one, even if you said the least in the room.
Praise colleagues to their manager. "Julia saved the project last week." It costs you nothing, it makes their day, and everyone wants to work with the guy who shares credit.
Ask for advice instead of help. "How would you approach this?" makes people feel respected, and they end up helping you far more than if you'd simply asked for a favour.
Before: nothing to say at the coffee machine. After: five minutes a day of history, art or science, and a fun story ready for every awkward break with colleagues.
slides.texte_sophia: Before: nothing to say at the coffee machine. After: five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. Now I've got a story for every break.

slides.texte_overlay: Answer messages fast, even with "Got it, I'll come back to you Friday." Quick acknowledgements make you look reliable, even when the real answer takes a few days.
Bring something back from your holidays. A box of local sweets on the office kitchen table. Tiny gesture, and the whole floor suddenly knows your name and smiles at you.
